added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent and identically distributed, and let \(\mathcal G\) be a pointwise-measurable \(\operatorname{VC}(b,a,v)\)-type class: \(|g|\le b\), \(a\ge e\), \(v\ge1\), and
\[
 \sup_Q N\{\mathcal G,L^2(Q),b\epsilon\}\le(a/\epsilon)^v,
 \qquad 0<\epsilon\le1.
\]
Suppose \(\sup_{g\in\mathcal G}E[g(X_1)^2]\le\sigma^2\le b^2\), let \(B\) be the tight centered Gaussian process with the covariance of \(g(X_1)-E[g(X_1)]\), and put
\[
 K_n=Av\{\log n\vee\log(ab/\sigma)\}\ge1.
\]
If \(W_n=\sup_{g\in\mathcal G}|n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\{g(X_i)-E[g(X_i)]\}|\), then for each \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) there is a coupling \(W^0\stackrel d=\sup_{g\in\mathcal G}|B(g)|\) such that
\[
 P\left\{|W_n-W^0|>
 \frac{bK_n}{(\gamma n)^{1/2}}+
 \frac{(b\sigma)^{1/2}K_n^{3/4}}{\gamma^{1/2}n^{1/4}}+
 \frac{b^{1/3}\sigma^{2/3}K_n^{2/3}}{\gamma^{1/3}n^{1/6}}
 \right\}
 \le A'\left(\gamma+\frac{\log n}{n}\right).
\]
For independent standard Gaussian multipliers, let \(\widetilde W_n(x_1^n)\) be the conditional supremum of the centered multiplier process. If, in addition,
\[
 b^2K_n\le n\sigma^2,
\]
and
\[
 \psi_n=\left(\frac{\sigma^2K_n}{n}\right)^{1/2}
 +\left(\frac{b^2\sigma^2K_n^3}{n}\right)^{1/4},
 \qquad
 \gamma_n(\delta)=\delta^{-1}
 \left(\frac{b^2\sigma^2K_n^3}{n}\right)^{1/4}+\frac1n,
\]
then for every \(\delta>0\) there is a measurable set \(S_{n,0}\) with \(P(X_1^n\in S_{n,0})\ge1-3/n\) such that, for every \(x_1^n\in S_{n,0}\), a coupling to the same law \(W^0\) satisfies
\[
 P\{|\widetilde W_n(x_1^n)-W^0|>\psi_n+\delta\}
 \le A''\gamma_n(\delta).
\]
Moreover, if \(X=(X_t)_{t\in T}\) is a centered separable Gaussian process with \(E[X_t^2]=1\) for every \(t\) and \(\sup_t|X_t|<\infty\) almost surely, then
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}P\left(\left|\sup_t|X_t|-x\right|\le\epsilon\right)
 \le4\epsilon\left\{E\sup_t|X_t|+1\right\}.
\]
Consequently, in a triangular application, distributional equivalence requires both that the empirical and conditional-multiplier coupling failure probabilities vanish uniformly and that the common coupling radius \(\epsilon_n\) satisfy \(\epsilon_n\{E\sup_t|B_n(t)|+1\}\to0\). In particular, when \(E\sup_t|B_n(t)|=O(\sqrt{\log n})\), the quantitative condition \(\epsilon_n\sqrt{\log n}\to0\) is sufficient; convergence of the radii without these probability and anti-concentration conditions is not sufficient.

source.locator: Appendix A, Theorems 5.1 and 5.2, together with Corollary 2.1
source.verbatim_statement: (Slepian--Stein type coupling for suprema of empirical processes): W^0\stackrel{d}{=}\Vert B\Vert_{\mathcal{G}}. (Slepian--Stein type coupling for suprema of conditional multiplier processes): b^2K_n\leq n\sigma^2. p_{\epsilon}(|X|)\leq4\epsilon(a(|X|)+1).

prose_updates.tldr: Under fixed order-\(k\) non-Gaussian treatment-noise separation, a noise-only finite contour bank yields quantitative moduli before the external-code radius is chosen.  Any frozen code whose conditional \(L^1\) remainder is at most \(\varepsilon_0\) after removal of an admissible Hölder modifier shift can then remain persistently imperfect: localized contour cancellation removes the arbitrary bounded baseline outcome regression without estimating it.  The resulting split-sample multiplier band is uniformly simultaneously honest for the causal slope curve and has expected supremum width \((\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\); an asymmetric Bernoulli exact-code Gaussian-regression subexperiment proves the matching lower bound over all measurable honest bands for every fixed \(k\ge3\).

project_justification.gap: Published uniform bands for heterogeneous or continuous-treatment causal functions rely on estimated pseudo-outcomes, outcome regressions, or balancing weights.  Existing separated non-Gaussian structure-agnostic results do not provide a modifier-indexed honest band under a fixed supplied-code remainder, and generic confidence-band theory does not by itself furnish the same-experiment all-measurable-band converse.
project_justification.niche: Independent additive non-Gaussian treatment noise supplies a transform winding certified by a law-independent finite bank.  A bounded Hölder modifier-only code displacement has zero winding after localization, while only its conditional direct remainder must be small; spectral cancellation then leaves Hölder variation of the causal treatment slope as the explicit localization bias.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the noise-only contour bank, attainment and strict enlargement of the modifier-shift code certificate, a uniform localized denominator modulus, reference-localized selector consistency, analytic baseline cancellation, an explicit Hölder-bias bound, a selected-contour Bahadur and multiplier theorem, a total honest band at the canonical Hölder width, and a matching many-bump converse over every measurable honest band.

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), inference is conditional on a deterministic external code \(\bar g_n\in\Gamma(P,\varepsilon_0)\) fixed before an independent and identically distributed sample; the sample is split deterministically into an independent pilot half for contour selection and an inference half for estimation and multiplier calibration.
sampling_model.units: The observed units \(O_i=(V_i,X_i,T_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), are independent and identically distributed from one law \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment obeys \(T=g_0(X,V)+\eta\), where \(\eta\perp(X,V)\), \(\eta\) is sub-Gaussian under the stated Luxemburg convention, and its fixed order-\(k\) cumulant has absolute value at least \(\delta>0\).
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity score is used.  The design density satisfies \(c_V\le f_V\le C_V\) on \([0,1]\).  The noise-only bank is derived first, \(\varepsilon_\star\) is computed from its maximal radius, and the fixed external-code radius satisfies \(0\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{app}}<\varepsilon_0\le\varepsilon_\star\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No outcome regression is estimated.  The result is conditional on a frozen external treatment code admitting a bounded Hölder modifier displacement whose residual conditional \(L^1\) error is at most \(\varepsilon_0\); it does not assert that this code or its certificate is learned from the inference sample.

prose_updates.related_work: Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017, Theorem 2 and Sections 2--4) obtain a doubly robust uniform conditional-treatment-effect band from estimated propensity and outcome regressions; their smoothing and inferential architecture informs this paper, but their pseudo-response does not address a persistently imperfect frozen treatment code.  Ai, Huang, and Zhang (2026, Sections 3--5 and Theorems 1--3) establish uniform Bahadur representations, bootstrap bands, and data-driven bias control for general continuous-treatment causal functions using estimated minimum-variance balancing weights.  There is no dominance claim in either direction: their model covers broad dose-response and loss-defined functionals without additive independent non-Gaussian residuals, whereas this paper studies a varying-coefficient slope under additive independent noise, fixed cumulant separation, localized contour cancellation, no outcome learner, and a fixed-radius supplied-code certificate; their paper does not give the all-honest-band expected-supremum-width converse proved here.  Fan and Zhang (2000, Theorem 2) give the classical varying-coefficient maximum-deviation benchmark.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014, Appendix A, Theorems 5.1 and 5.2, and Corollary 2.1) supply the empirical-process coupling, conditional multiplier coupling, and Gaussian anti-concentration interface after the new contour-ratio linearization.  Low (1997) and Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) inform the testing-to-width and explicit-bias logic.  Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) settle Hölder heterogeneous-effect estimation rates but not honest expected supremum width under fixed external-code error.  Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis (2025) inform the separated non-Gaussian structure-agnostic regime, but not a uniform treatment-slope band with the modifier-shift conditional-remainder certificate used here.  Chen and Christensen (2018) and Babii (2020) inform the weak-separation question through inverse-problem conditioning rather than serving as dominance targets.
prose_updates.interpretation: The causal target is the structural treatment-slope curve \(\tau_0(v)\), not the contour functional or its sample analogue.  On a selected denominator-safe contour, \(\Theta_{v,h}\) is a computable localized population functional: analytic contour integration cancels the arbitrary bounded baseline outcome regression, exactly recovers every constant slope, and differs from \(\tau_0(v)\) by at most \(B_{\mathrm{bias}}L_\tau h^\beta\).  The sample center \(\widehat\tau_n(v)\) estimates \(\Theta_{v,h_n}\); adding the explicit bias allowance converts multiplier coverage for that smoothed functional into simultaneous coverage for the causal curve.  Balancing stochastic width and Hölder bias at \(h_n\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2\beta+1)}\) yields the minimax expected supremum-width rate.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The shrinking-width theorem uses fixed positive cumulant separation.  Its constants can deteriorate through the bank radius and boundary modulus as separation weakens, and the present primitives do not identify a sharp \(\delta_n\)-dependent rate.  Over the natural vanishing-separation enlargement, the proved result is only the honest bracket between the Hölder lower order \(r_n\) and the constant-width band \(2C_\tau\).  The procedure also presumes an externally fixed code satisfying the modifier-shift conditional-remainder certificate; certification or learning of that code is outside the theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The closed fixed-separation results take \(\beta\in(0,1]\) and its Hölder radius as known, work on an interior one-dimensional modifier interval, assume the displayed density, range, tail, variance, independence, and fixed cumulant conditions, and are uniform over law--code pairs with \(0\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{app}}<\varepsilon_0\le\varepsilon_\star\).  The probability-law class remains distinct from the external-code input, and no auxiliary-sample learning guarantee is claimed.  The exact-code asymmetric Bernoulli subclass embeds ordinary uniform-design Gaussian nonparametric regression for every fixed \(k\ge3\), which makes the all-band lower bound valid over the same pair class.  Unknown-smoothness adaptation, boundary inference, multivariate modifiers, and sharp weak-separation behavior remain outside the closed theorem.

statement_notes.justification: The lemma produces a finite contour bank and quantitative transform moduli solely from \((k,\delta,\psi_\eta)\), so the admissible code-error radius is chosen afterward without circularity.
statement_notes.gap: Separated finite-order non-Gaussian estimation and a scalar contour identity do not provide the localized band's required noise-only quantitative ordering.
statement_notes.consumer: All denominator, selector, bias, and multiplier arguments use these bank outputs.

statement_notes.justification: Pilot selection may choose a bank contour other than the population certificate, so the treatment-transform derivative must be controlled uniformly over the whole finite bank.
statement_notes.gap: A bound only on the certified contour does not control the data-selected contour.
statement_notes.consumer: The localized bias proof combines this envelope with the selected localized-denominator modulus.

statement_notes.justification: Compactness makes the modifier-shift certificate operational, while the inclusion and constant-shift witness show that it genuinely enlarges the direct conditional-error class.
statement_notes.gap: A direct conditional-\(L^1\) ball excludes persistent modifier-only displacement even though that displacement is spectrally removable.
statement_notes.consumer: The robustness proof selects an attained displacement witness for every admissible external code.

statement_notes.justification: The shift-factorization inequality turns fixed residual error and a Hölder modifier displacement into a uniform localized denominator modulus and a winding-zero code factor.
statement_notes.gap: Neither an unconditional error criterion nor a global contaminated transform protects every modifier-localized denominator.
statement_notes.consumer: Selection, contour bias, and inference all use the resulting \(\rho_F\) modulus.

statement_notes.justification: The lemma makes the population contour certificate operational through a reference-localized pilot winding test and a uniform localized boundary test.
statement_notes.gap: Generic band coupling does not control a data-selected complex contour or separate its winding from modifier displacement.
statement_notes.consumer: The independent inference half conditions on the same contour, winding, and denominator modulus used by the estimator.

statement_notes.justification: Analytic cancellation removes the bounded baseline outcome regression, constant slopes are recovered exactly, and the only remaining deterministic error is an explicit Hölder localization bias.
statement_notes.gap: Classical varying-coefficient smoothing does not supply a modifier-shift-robust contour-bias envelope.
statement_notes.consumer: The explicit bias allowance yields target-curve coverage without undersmoothing or an outcome learner.

statement_notes.justification: The cited interface records the exact empirical coupling, conditional multiplier coupling, envelope condition, failure probabilities, and Gaussian anti-concentration inequality used in the triangular score-process application.
statement_notes.gap: A qualitative appeal to multiplier validity would omit the load-bearing envelope condition and the requirement that coupling radii vanish on the Gaussian anti-concentration scale.
statement_notes.consumer: The selected-contour Bahadur lemma verifies this interface for truncated and studentized localized influence scores.

statement_notes.justification: The lemma derives the selected-contour ratio linearization, nondegenerate variance, plug-in studentization, empirical and multiplier couplings, fallback probabilities, and critical-value moment bound.
statement_notes.gap: Generic multiplier theory starts from a valid indexed linearization; it does not create one for a pilot-selected localized contour ratio under fixed code remainder.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies both simultaneous calibration and the stochastic expected-width bound.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem gives whole-curve simultaneous coverage and the canonical Hölder expected-width rate under a fixed positive-radius external-code certificate and no outcome learner.
statement_notes.gap: Existing causal-function bands use fitted regression or weighting nuisances rather than localized spectral cancellation with a persistently imperfect frozen treatment code.
statement_notes.consumer: A study with a fixed certified treatment predictor can report an honest treatment-slope curve band without fitting \(q_0\).

statement_notes.justification: The asymmetric two-point treatment residual gives a nonzero order-\(k\) cumulant and a valid Gaussian-regression reduction for every \(k\ge3\), including odd orders.
statement_notes.gap: A symmetric Rademacher residual cannot certify odd-order cumulant separation.
statement_notes.consumer: The proposition embeds the standard Gaussian Hölder experiment used by the all-band converse.

statement_notes.justification: The explicit disjoint-location bump family supplies same-class sup-norm separation and logarithmic Kullback--Leibler control.
statement_notes.gap: A generic testing-to-length theorem does not construct the required location family inside this causal law--code experiment.
statement_notes.consumer: The family is the least-favorable input to the all-measurable-band width lower bound.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem proves that the simultaneous logarithmic price is information-limited and matches the spectral band's upper rate.
statement_notes.gap: Classical regression-band results do not directly establish expected supremum-width optimality over this law--external-code pair class.
statement_notes.consumer: The reported width is minimax optimal even against nonspectral, asymmetric, and variable-width measurable bands.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem records the strongest consequence of the unchanged primitives when cumulant separation vanishes: the fixed-class Hölder lower order persists, while the deterministic range band gives a universal constant upper bound.
statement_notes.gap: The current bank and coupling bounds do not yield a sharp stability modulus or shrinking-width threshold as \(\delta_n\downarrow0\).
statement_notes.consumer: It separates the closed fixed-separation theorem from the unresolved weak-to-Gaussian transition without overstating a \(\delta_n\)-dependent rate.
